summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes and chronic back pain was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by worsening back pain and hyperglycemia. She presented with nausea, vomiting, and critically high blood glucose. IV fluids and insulin were initiated, with successful stabilization of her metabolic parameters. She was treated for an asymptomatic E. coli urinary tract infection with ciprofloxacin. Nausea improved with Zofran and metoclopramide, and she resumed a regular diet. Persistent daytime tachycardia, likely related to pain and anxiety, improved with supportive care. Psychiatry restarted sertraline for depression. She was discharged home on her baseline insulin regimen with follow-up plans for diabetes, pain, and mental health management.
